svg.title: Reverse proxy · tokens stay in Redis
svg.desc: NGINX is the public edge; oauth2-proxy handles OIDC and session lookup.
svg.text: 03 / CONFIDENTIAL CLIENT
Reverse proxy · tokens stay in Redis
NGINX is the public edge; oauth2-proxy handles OIDC and session lookup.
Browser
Same-origin React UI
Opaque cookie ticket
Reverse proxy
NGINX + oauth2-proxy
Client: proxy · Redis
Keycloak
workshop realm
Identity provider
Orders API
Protected resource
aud: orders-api
Start proxy login
/oauth2/start sends the browser to Keycloak.
Sign in with the proxy client
Browser follows the redirect with state and an S256 PKCE challenge.
Return the code through the browser
Browser follows /oauth2/callback to oauth2-proxy via NGINX.
Redeem the code with oauth2-proxy
Server sends the code + PKCE verifier + confidential-client authentication.
Store the OIDC session in Redis
Keycloak returns OAuth tokens; oauth2-proxy stores the session server-side.
Give the browser an opaque session ticket
Set the Secure, HttpOnly _oauth2_proxy cookie; no OAuth tokens.
Request the same-origin API
/api/orders uses the cookie; writes require exact Origin + X-Workshop-CSRF: 1.
Validate the session inside the proxy
Internal auth_request checks the cookie and restores the Redis session.
NGINX → oauth2-proxy → Redis
Inject the access token only upstream
NGINX removes /api, replaces Authorization and strips browser cookies.
Return application data through NGINX
Orders enforces its JWT and role checks; auth-subrequest token headers stay private.
TOKEN BOUNDARY
Browser holds an opaque cookie ticket.
OAuth tokens stay in the Redis session.
Redis is ephemeral in this workshop.
ORDERS MAKES THE DECISION
Validate JWT signature, issuer, expiry
and audience; then enforce realm roles.
Solid arrows: requests • Dashed arrows: responses / browser callbacks
